item.title: Vector Quantized Information Bottleneck Mitigation of Adversarial Attacks on Modulation Classifiers
item.description: arXiv:2611.33456v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Radio-frequency (RF) signal processing based on machine learning, including Automatic Modulation Classification (AMC), plays a critical role in Next Generation (NextG) intelligent communications but remains highly vulnerable to adversarial attacks. Prior work explored Variational Information Bottleneck (VIB) as a means to improve robustness, but only in continuous spaces and never for RF classifiers. We investigate the impact of discrete-space information bottlenecks on the adversarial robustness of AMC models. Classification accuracy of attacked modulated RF waveforms is evaluated in two frameworks designed to leverage VIB for adversarial robustness: (i) a two-stage framework where VIB is applied in the preprocessing step using a Vector Quantized Variational Autoencoder (VQVAE) to suppress adversarial perturbations in the process of input signal reconstruction and (ii) a Vector Quantized Classifier (VQC) that leverages VIB inside the classifier proper. The architectures of VQVAE and VQC are identical up to the bottleneck where the VQVAE adds a decoder while VQC utilizes a classification head. We train both VQVAE and VQC with loss functions that we derive from the VIB information-theoretic model. Both frameworks incorporate vector quantization and KL regularization to enforce discrete bottlenecks that filter out adversarial noise. Evaluations under white-box attacks demonstrate that discrete bottlenecks significantly enhance robustness: VQVAE outperforms its continuous VAE (Variational Autoencoder) counterpart, while VQC achieves strong robustness without requiring signal reconstruction.
item.dc:creator: Attanasia Garuso, Silvija Kokalj-Filipovic

item.title: Exact Minimum Distances of Primitive Narrow-Sense BCH Codes: At and Beyond the Bose Distance
item.description: arXiv:2611.33613v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We determine the exact minimum distances of two families of primitive narrow-sense BCH codes of length $q^m-1$, where $q$ is a prime power and $m\geq 4$. For $1\leq i\leq\lfloor m/2\rfloor$, codes with designed distance $q^m-q^{m-1}-q^{m-1-i}-1$ have minimum distance and Bose distance both equal to their designed distance. Furthermore, for integers $\ell, i, s$ satisfying $3\leq\ell<m-1$ and $\lfloor m/(\ell+1)\rfloor\leq i\leq s<\lfloor(m-1)/\ell\rfloor$, codes with designed distance $q^m-q^{m-1}-q^{m-1-i}-q^s-1$ have Bose distance equal to their designed distance and minimum distance $q^m-q^{m-1}-q^{m-1-i}-1$. Consequently, the gap between the minimum distance and the Bose distance in this family is exactly $q^s$ and grows without bound as $m$ increases, with fixed $\ell$.The proofs proceed by constructing good zero-sets from quadratic forms for the first family, and by combining upper bounds provided by the first family with lower bounds derived from the divisibility of codeword weights in punctured generalized Reed--Muller codes for the second. We also derive explicit dimension formulas by counting cyclotomic cosets.
item.dc:creator: Run Zheng

item.title: Quantization and Codebook Stability of Euclidean and KL Lattice Quantizers
item.description: arXiv:2611.33811v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Small edits to raw data can cause large changes in the compressed version, which can be costly in applications such as data synchronization and incremental backup. We study quantization stability, the probability that two perturbed distributions map to the same representative, and codebook stability, the probability that the resulting Huffman codebooks are the same. We first quantize the empirical distribution and then construct a Huffman code from the quantized distribution, which can improve codebook stability at the cost of some compression efficiency. We study two quantizers based on a shifted and scaled lattice in the probability simplex: the Euclidean Lattice Quantizer (ELQ) and the KL Quantizer (KLQ). For ELQ, we derive bounds on quantization stability and KL distortion. For KLQ, we show that its quantization cells can be determined by comparisons with adjacent lattice codewords and use the distances to the cell boundaries to derive a quantization stability bound. For a symmetric codebook of positive types, we obtain the exact worst-case KL distortion over the full probability simplex. We also give a heuristic choice $\alpha^\star$ of the minimum codeword probability and compare it with the minimum coordinate of a Lloyd-optimized codebook. Simulations using canonical Huffman coding compare ELQ and KLQ with an existing compander-based quantizer and show the trade-off between KL distortion, codebook stability, and encoded length under random deletions.
item.dc:creator: Haoxuan Luo, Ryan Gabrys, Farzad Farnoud

item.title: Certified Outage Bounds for RIS-Assisted NOMA with Source-Side Thermal Energy Harvesting
item.description: arXiv:2611.33986v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Gaussian useful-gain and mean-interference approximations can cause opposite power-sizing errors in reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-assisted non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA). We extend a source-side thermal energy harvesting model with Poisson interference and certify two-sided outage bounds. In a tested environment, the combined required signal-to-noise ratio error has opposite signs at 20 and 24 elements per user. Under another power convention, mean or moment-matched Gamma-distributed interference can predict false feasibility with exact useful gain. In the Gamma case, the Gaussian gain approximation can mask this false feasibility. Propagated Chernoff bounds give sufficient designs. Results concern the specified model and tested regimes.
item.dc:creator: Victor Rabiet (MIC, ENS-PSL)

item.title: Semantic Tanner-Graph Decoding for LDPC Codes
item.description: arXiv:2611.34175v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Conventional low-density parity-check (LDPC) belief propagation (BP) decoding operates on a Tanner graph, with no factor describing the source structure. This paper proposes a semantic Tanner graph for LDPC-coded text transmission and develops semantic-factor-aided BP (SF-BP) decoding. The source text is tokenized into discrete tokens, which are then mapped to binary messages for channel coding. For each token, the proposed graph introduces a semantic factor connected to the corresponding information-bit variable nodes forming the token. A fine-tuned language model assigns this factor a posterior distribution over all possible token symbols in the alphabet at each token position. During SF-BP decoding, semantic-factor and LDPC parity-check messages are combined at their shared variable nodes for message passing. Simulation results show that SF-BP significantly improves the block error rate (BLER) and Sentence-BERT similarity (BERT: Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers) compared with conventional BP. For example, SF-BP reduces BLER from approximately 1 to 6.51 x 10^-6 and increases Sentence-BERT similarity from 0.21 to 1 - 1.26 x 10^-6 for the (1248, 1040) LDPC code at 4 dB.
item.dc:creator: Wenjing Wei, Chentao Yue, Branka Vucetic, Yonghui Li

item.title: Several classes of few-weight linear codes based on Weil sums
item.description: arXiv:2611.34267v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Linear codes over finite fields with few weights are of significant interest due to their applications in areas such as secret sharing schemes, strongly regular graphs, and association schemes. In this paper, we construct several classes of p-ary linear codes based on Weil sums via the defining-set construction of bivariate form, where p is an odd prime. Utilizing the theory of quadratic forms and Weil sums over finite fields, the parameters and weight distributions of the codes are completely determined. As a result, several families of three-weight or four-weight linear codes are obtained from our construction. In addition, it is shown that most of our codes are minimal.
item.dc:creator: Lan Deng (Hubei Key Laboratory of Applied Mathematics, Faculty of Mathematics and Statistics, Hubei University, Wuhan, China, School of Mathematics and Statistics, Hanjiang Normal University, Shiyan, China), Zhao Hu (Key Laboratory of Intelligent Sensing System and Security), Nian Li (Key Laboratory of Intelligent Sensing System and Security)

item.title: Simulation-Assisted Radio Map Reconstruction with Sparse Field Measurements
item.description: arXiv:2611.33202v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Field measurements are essential for evaluating radio map reconstruction under real-world conditions, but their acquisition is costly. This letter proposes a simulation-assisted parameterized-background data-weak (SA-PBDW) method that combines propagation simulations with sparse field measurements, which jointly estimates background coefficients and a spatial correction to account for discrepancies between simulated and measured power distributions. Dense field measurements are collected for multiple transmitter positions at an urban site. Evaluations on the collected data and RadioMapSeer demonstrate improved reconstruction accuracy and structural fidelity over benchmark methods at reduced sampling rates.
item.dc:creator: Lang Ming, Longhui Wang, Yazhou Sun, Xi Chen, Jian Wang, Yu Wang

item.title: Sharp one-shot bounds and optimal exponents of universal randomness extraction
item.description: arXiv:2611.33270v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce techniques for the study of randomness extraction against quantum side information (privacy amplification) by relating this problem to variants of hypothesis testing tasks with quadratic constraints. Building also on the recently introduced measured smooth entropy approach of [Regula and Tomamichel, arXiv:2603.04493], we precisely determine the optimal scaling of the error of quantum privacy amplification in several regimes. Our results apply to the standard operational security criterion based on trace distance and focus in particular on universal classes of hash functions. On the technical side, our investigation reveals connections with operator space theory methods used in non-commutative Khintchine inequalities. As one application, we give a one-shot converse bound that shows the leftover hash lemma of [arXiv:2603.04493] to be tight up to a constant factor for all strongly 4-universal hash functions. This allows us to evaluate the asymptotic i.i.d. error exponent of universal randomness extraction for all rates, matching the bound of [Dupuis, arXiv:2105.05342] and improving also earlier classical asymptotic results of [Hayashi, arXiv:1010.1358]. We furthermore give new one-shot achievability and converse bounds on the error in the strong converse regime, which we show to match up to a constant factor. This establishes the exact strong converse exponent of quantum privacy amplification under 2-universal hash functions, complementing the converse bound of [Shen, Gao, and Cheng, arXiv:2202.10263].
item.dc:creator: Bartosz Regula, Hao-Chung Cheng

item.title: What Must LLM Agents Communicate? From Information Loss to Communication Failures
item.description: arXiv:2611.33318v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: When evidence is distributed across LLM agents, a team may collectively possess all the information needed for a decision yet fail to use it effectively. What must agents communicate for accurate joint predictions, and when does interaction help? We study three requirements for effective communication: sufficiency of the information conveyed, selection of relevant evidence, and utilization of received information. Drawing on information theory and communication complexity, we develop a framework that combines theoretical benchmarks with controlled experiments and message-level analyses. We find that local probability reports can discard essential information, with theoretical information loss closely matching observed performance penalties. Query-first interaction improves predictions when relevant evidence depends on a private query, but compact one-shot representations can eliminate this advantage. Even when sufficient information is communicated, agents may fail to select or use it correctly. Together, these findings distinguish fundamental communication limits from failures in how LLM agents communicate and use information.
item.dc:creator: Yi-Yun Chu, Xiaobin Shen

item.title: Universal Work Extraction from Individual Sequences by Finite--State Information Engines
item.description: arXiv:2611.33984v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider information engines that interact with a heat bath at temperature $T$, a work reservoir, and a tape carrying an individual (deterministic) sequence $x$ over a finite alphabet $\X$. An engine is a cascade of autonomous ratchets with fixed energy levels and detailed--balance dynamics, each processing segments of $m$ tape cells and having finitely many internal states. We prove a converse bound on the extractable work in terms of the empirical block entropies of $x$,and show that it is achievable \emph{universally}, by engines whose energy levels do not depend on $x$. The maximal work per symbol is $kT[\ln|\X|-\bar H(x)]$, where $k$ is Boltzmann's constant and $\bar H(x)$ is the asymptotic normalized aligned block entropy of $x$, which equals its block Lempel--Ziv complexity, and the minimal work needed to erase $x$ is $kT\bar H(x)$ per symbol. Underlying these results is a two--way correspondence with universal coding: energy levels define a code, and a suitably operated cascade extracts $kT$ times $\ln|\X|$ per symbol minus the code length; conversely, a fluctuation identity shows that every engine fixed in advance defines a code. Hence, converses of universal coding apply verbatim to engines; e.g., the optimal redundancy of memoryless universal engines is given by the Shtarkov sum.
item.dc:creator: Neri Merhav

item.title: Quantum Advantage in Privacy-Preserving Hypothesis Testing via Entanglement-Assisted Classical Communication
item.description: arXiv:2611.34029v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Quantum mechanisms satisfying quantum local differential privacy (QLDP) have been shown to achieve a quantum advantage over classical local differential privacy (LDP) mechanisms in certain hypothesis-testing problems. While previous demonstrations have considered the transmission of quantum states from users to a server, we investigate whether this advantage can persist under entanglement-assisted classical communication (EACC), where users and the server share entanglement in advance and communicate only classical messages. We formulate an EACC-based hypothesis-testing framework and introduce measurement local differential privacy (MLDP) to protect private inputs against arbitrary shared quantum states and server-side measurements. We establish that QLDP classical-to-quantum channels admit MLDP-compliant EACC simulations and that, in the high-privacy regime, certain optimal QLDP mechanisms can be realized with one-bit classical communication, albeit using high-dimensional entanglement. We then demonstrate that a strict quantum advantage persists even when the pre-shared entanglement is restricted to a single qubit pair and each user communicates only one classical bit. Using EACC protocols based on the geometry of qubit measurements, we establish this advantage for both asymmetric and symmetric hypothesis testing and every input alphabet of size $v \geq 3$ in the high-privacy limit. The ratio of the achieved error exponent to the optimal one under the LDP constraint is at least $5/4$ for all such alphabets and approaches $3/2$ as $v$ grows. These results demonstrate that quantum advantage in locally private hypothesis testing can persist under simultaneous constraints on entanglement dimension and classical communication.
item.dc:creator: Ji-Ho Jung, Seung-Hyun Nam, Si-Hyeon Lee

item.title: Revisiting Unicity Distance: A Channel Transmission Perspective and Its Limits
item.description: arXiv:2410.14816v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper revisits the classical notion of unicity distance for substitution ciphers from an information-theoretic perspective. We frame simple-substitution encryption as a noisy transmission channel, in which the plaintext is the message, the unknown key is the noise, and the attacker is the receiver. Using typical sets to motivate the notion of meaningful plaintexts, we apply the channel coding theorem to blocks of plaintext encrypted with independent fresh keys. We show that a block length exceeding $H(K)/D$ permits reliable communication at the language's entropy rate using suitably chosen codebooks across many blocks. This provides a channel transmission interpretation of the classical unicity-distance formula. We then test how well this formula describes plaintext recovery when the message is a passage from six known novels. More than $99\%$ of the passages are uniquely identifiable at 18 letters, well before the classical estimate of about 28. N-gram language models, based on the frequencies of short letter sequences, predict the recovery probabilities much more closely. Hellman (1977) warned that the classical estimate can overstate security, but not by how much. Here it is off by about ten letters.
item.dc:creator: Fangyuan Lin

item.title: A Note on Binary Quadratic Systems and their relation to complexity theory
item.description: arXiv:2609.07769v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Deciding whether a system of multivariate quadratic equations over $\mathbb F_2$ has a solution is a classical NP-complete problem, and remains so for square systems, with as many equations as variables. The hardness of this problem is one of the cornerstones of nowadays post-quantum cryptography. Let $\mathrm{MQ}_0(n)$ and $\mathrm{MQ}_1(n)$ denote the sets of square quadratic systems in $n$ variables having respectively no solutions and exactly one solution. $\cup_{n\geq 2} \mathrm{MQ}_0(n)$ is a coNP-complete language, while $\cup_{n\geq 2} \mathrm{MQ}_1(n)$ lies in DP. It is known that $\lim_{n\to \infty} |\mathrm{MQ}_1(n)|/|\mathrm{MQ}_0(n)|=1$. Here we prove the explicit finite-$n$ bounds \[ |\mathrm{MQ}_0(n)|<|\mathrm{MQ}_1(n)| \le \left(1+\frac{1}{2^n-1}\right)|\mathrm{MQ}_0(n)|, \] More generally, let $Q_d$ be the space of polynomial functions $(\mathbb{F}_2)^n\to\mathbb F_2$ of degree at most $d$, and let $\alpha_k$ count square systems in $(Q_d)^n$ having exactly $k$ solutions. Then \[ \alpha_0<\alpha_1 \le \left(1+\frac{1}{2^n-1}\right)\alpha_0\,, \qquad 2\le d\le n \,. \] The proof combines matroid and coding-theoretic methods. We interpret $(\mathbb{F}_2)^n$ as the ground set of the evaluation matroid of $Q_d$, express $\alpha_0$ and $\alpha_1$ through characteristic polynomials, and use a Whitney-type sign-reversing involution to show that the only terms that can push $\alpha_1-\alpha_0$ below $\alpha_1/2^n$ come from the elements of a matroid port. These are identified with minimal-support words of the Reed--Muller code $\mathrm{RM}(n-d-1,n)=\mathrm{RM}(d,n)^\perp$; the required estimate then follows from the MacWilliams identity, the minimum-distance bound $2^{d+1}$, and the even-weight structure of the code.
item.dc:creator: Gabriele Radici, Massimiliano Sala

item.title: Uniform Sampling of Linear Codes with Prescribed Hull Dimension
item.description: arXiv:2611.03578v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We give exactly uniform samplers for linear codes with prescribed hull dimension, for the Euclidean, Hermitian, and symplectic inner products and over finite fields of every characteristic. Except for the Euclidean form over fields of odd characteristic, these are the first uniform samplers for arbitrary prescribed hull dimension. Each sample costs an expected $O(k^2 N + k \log q)$ field operations for codes of dimension $k$ in a space of dimension $N$ over $\mathbb{F}_q$ or $\mathbb{F}_{q^2}$.
item.dc:creator: Keita Ishizuka

item.title: Gaussian mass inequalities for lattices
item.description: arXiv:2611.19749v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Gaussian mass of a lattice is the evaluation of its theta series at a real nome and is relevant to lattice coding for the wiretap Gaussian channel. The ratio of the Gaussian mass of stable lattices to the Gaussian mass of the integer lattice was conjectured to be $\le 1$ (Regev et al., 2024). Kominers proved this bound recently for lattices obtained by Construction~A from binary self-dual codes. Building on Kominers' bound, we establish corresponding inequalities on average for Construction~$A_4$ lattices obtained from free self-dual quaternary codes and for Construction~$A_6$ lattices obtained from self-dual senary codes. We also prove the strict Gaussian-mass inequality for extremal unimodular lattices of both Type~II and Type~I. The Type~I result uses the Rains--Sloane definition of extremality. Its proof combines a universal theta truncation with an exact inversion of the shadow coefficients, and a Gaussian inequality for translated lattices. In addition, we obtain an averaging bound over the genus of Type~II lattices, and extend the binary Construction~A inequality to Siegel theta series of arbitrary genus, with further quaternary results under conditions on the residue code.
item.dc:creator: Minjia Shi, Xinguang Dai, Patrick Sol\'e

item.title: Relative Entropy under Ordered Chi-Squared Constraints: Sharp Bounds and Extremizers
item.description: arXiv:2611.24607v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We derive a sharp upper bound on the relative entropy $D(P\|Q)$ in terms of the two ordered chi-squared divergences $\chi^2(P\|Q)$ and $\chi^2(Q\|P)$. For any $A,B>0$, the constraints $\chi^2(P\|Q)\leq A$ and $\chi^2(Q\|P)\leq B$ yield upper bounds on $D(P\|Q)$ and $D(Q\|P)$. Two pairs of Bernoulli distributions each attain both bounds simultaneously. As a consequence, for sequences of probability mass functions $\{P_n\}$ and $\{Q_n\}$ on a common finite or countably infinite alphabet, both $D(P_n\|Q_n)$ and $D(Q_n\|P_n)$ tend to zero whenever one of the two ordered chi-squared divergences tends to zero and the other remains uniformly bounded. Without this boundedness assumption, $D(P_n\|Q_n)$ can fail to converge to zero even when $\chi^2(Q_n\|P_n)\to 0$. Finally, in contrast to the attainable upper bounds, on any finite or countably infinite alphabet containing at least three elements, the infimum of $D(P\|Q)$ under the exact constraints $\chi^2(P\|Q)=A$ and $\chi^2(Q\|P)=B$ is zero and is not attained. As an application to lossless source coding, we consider the product measures $P^n$ and $Q^n$ induced by $P$ and $Q$, respectively, on blocks of length $n$. We bound the expected saving in ideal codelength under $P^n$ when the encoder replaces $Q^n$ with the mixture $\lambda P^n+(1-\lambda)Q^n$. The lower bound depends on the sources only through $D(P\|Q)$, and the upper bound depends on them only through the two ordered chi-squared divergences between $P$ and $Q$. For every fixed $n$, the upper bound agrees with the expected saving to first order as $\lambda \to 0^+$.
item.dc:creator: Igal Sason

item.title: Practical limitations on robustness and scalability of quantum Internet
item.description: arXiv:2308.12739v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The realization of a desirably functional quantum Internet is hindered by fundamental and practical challenges such as high loss during transmission of quantum systems, decoherence due to interaction with the environment, fragility of quantum states under measurement, etc. We study the implications of these constraints by analyzing the limitations on the scaling and robustness of the quantum Internet. Considering quantum networks, we present practical bottlenecks for secure communication, delegated computing, and resource distribution among end nodes. In particular, we show that the device-independent quantum key distribution (DI-QKD) network of isotropic states with parameter $p$ has a finite diameter depending on $p$. Motivated by the power of abstraction in graph theory (in association with quantum information theory), that allows us to consider the topology of a network of users spatially separated over long distances around the globe or separated as nodes within the small space over a processor or circuit within a same framework, we consider graph-theoretic quantifiers to assess network robustness and provide critical values of communication lines for viable communication over quantum Internet. We consider some quantum networks of practical interest, ranging from satellite-based networks connecting far-off spatial locations to currently available quantum processor architectures within computers, and analyze their robustness to perform quantum information processing tasks. Some of these tasks form primitives for delegated quantum computing, e.g., entanglement distribution and quantum teleportation, that are desirable for all scale of quantum networks, be it quantum processors or quantum Internet.
item.dc:creator: Abhishek Sadhu, Meghana Ayyala Somayajula, Karol Horodecki, Siddhartha Das

item.title: Biologically Inspired Coordination of Parameter Selection and Update Strength for Language Model Adaptation
item.description: arXiv:2604.00533v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Adapting a source-trained language model to a target task requires deciding which parameters to update and how strongly when learning signals are uncertain. We introduce Synapse Consolidation (SyCo), a biologically inspired framework that coordinates these two controls. Rac1-associated forgetting and memory-trace redistribution motivate retaining selected source-derived low-rank components while resetting others for target adaptation. MAPK-associated signal processing motivates combining multiple prediction-based indicators over time to regulate update strength. SyCo combines these controls with a structured consistency objective and a small, fixed buffer of labelled source examples. Target labels are not used during adaptation. We evaluate the framework in Multi-source Open-set Adaptation (MOA), using source-initialized target learners for tasks absent from source training and for perturbed held-out inputs from source tasks. Across 18 natural-language-processing datasets, SyCo reaches 78.01% average accuracy on unseen-task adaptation and 85.37% under unseen-data shifts, outperforming the strongest evaluated hybrid baselines. Ablations support complementary contributions from selective plasticity, evidence-guided update control and structured consistency. These results show how coordinated control of update location and strength can improve target adaptation under uncertain learning signals.
item.dc:creator: Xiao Zhang, Tianyu Hu, Juntao Lyu, Qianchuan Zhao, Huimin Ma

item.title: Near-Optimal Learning of Gaussian Sobolev Operators
item.description: arXiv:2607.11921v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A key question in operator learning is how to design surrogate operators with provable approximation guarantees in reasonable computational time. Whereas holomorphic operators can be approximated efficiently, i.e., with at least algebraic convergence in the number of training samples, learning finitely regular operators is known to be less efficient. The reason is an intrinsic curse of sample complexity, which allows only subalgebraic convergence rates. This fact makes it all the more important to develop algorithms which provably achieve these rates. In this work, we present a fully data-driven algorithm, termed Hermite-PCA approximation, for learning Gaussian Sobolev operators with near-optimal sample complexity. It employs principal component analysis and weighted least-squares methods and is therefore computationally efficient. Moreover, it is spectral, in the sense that it achieves faster (and near-optimal) convergence as the Sobolev regularity increases. We provide a full error analysis of this algorithm along with numerical experiments that match our theoretical results and empirically confirm the efficacy of Hermite-PCA approximation for learning Sobolev operators.
item.dc:creator: Ben Adcock, Michael Griebel, Gregor Maier

item.title: Fundamental Limits of Query-Based Subgraph Detection
item.description: arXiv:2607.17118v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The planted subgraph detection problem asks whether a random graph contains a hidden structured subgraph. In the classical formulation, the entire adjacency matrix is observed and one distinguishes between an Erd\H{o}s--R\'enyi random graph and one obtained by planting a copy of a prescribed graph inside an Erd\H{o}s--R\'enyi random graph. The statistical and computational limits of this problem under full observation are now well understood, even for arbitrary planted subgraphs. In this paper, we investigate an information-limited version of the problem in which the planted structure is an arbitrary sequence of graphs $\Gamma=(\Gamma_n)_{n\geq1}$, where $\Gamma_n$ is embedded in an ambient graph on $n$ vertices, but the observer does not have access to the full adjacency matrix. Instead, information is acquired through a limited number of non-adaptive edge queries. We study the minimum query complexity required for reliable detection. We derive general information-theoretic lower bounds and algorithmic upper bounds on the query complexity as functions of the query budget and structural properties of the planted graph. The proposed algorithms exploit three distinct structural mechanisms: dense local motifs, high-degree vertices, and global edge density. We establish matching bounds, up to polylogarithmic factors, for several broad families of planted graphs, including clique-like, bounded-cover, and hub-dominated graph classes, as well as complete bipartite graphs of arbitrary aspect ratio. Our framework substantially generalizes existing query-complexity results for planted clique and planted dense subgraph models, providing a unified treatment of arbitrary planted subgraphs under restricted graph access.
item.dc:creator: Wasim Huleihel

item.title: Simultaneous Reduction of Observables and Measured Qudits in Entanglement-Assisted Quantum Local Recovery
item.description: arXiv:2609.23316v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $\mathbb{F}_q$ be the finite field with $q$ elements, $q$ being a prime power. For an entanglement-assisted or unassisted stabilizer code defined by an $\mathbb{F}_q$-linear space $C\subseteq\mathbb{F}_q^{2n}$, a set of erasures and an associated repair group, we propose a procedure to compute a reduced set of observables and a reduced repair group of codeword qudits for correcting the given erasures. The computed set of observables has the smallest possible size for correcting the given erasures, within the stabilizer measurement model. The repair group is reduced by eliminating qudits that need not be measured. In classical local recovery, such symbols can be found by Gaussian elimination, although the resulting repair group need not be a smallest one. In the quantum case we eliminate an admissible set of qudits. Finding a largest admissible set is a linear matroid parity problem, and for Calderbank--Shor--Steane (CSS) codes defined by two linear codes it is a linear matroid intersection problem. Both problems are solvable in deterministic polynomial time. We give closed-form upper bounds on the size of reduced repair groups for general codes and for codes from Euclidean and Hermitian orthogonality, and, for two-code CSS codes, a sharper bound with a min--max formula. Based on these bounds, we propose quantum counterparts of the concept of dimension locality of classical local recovery.
item.dc:creator: Carlos Galindo, Fernando Hernando, Ryutaroh Matsumoto

item.title: Even Sharper Bounds for Transductive Learning and Its Applications
item.description: arXiv:2609.28459v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We introduce Sharper Transductive Local Complexity (STLC) as a new tool for improving current transductive bounds. Although Local Rademacher Complexity (LRC) has been used to obtain sharp inductive generalization bounds and local-complexity-based transductive bounds, it has remained open whether a localized Rademacher-complexity framework can achieve the same fixed-point and confidence structure as its inductive counterpart. STLC provides an affirmative answer to this question. STLC is constructed by first deriving a new Bernstein-type concentration inequality for the test-train process, under uniform sampling without replacement. The proof uses a new two-parameter entropy argument based on the modified log-Sobolev inequality for the swap walk. A subsequent peeling strategy with a surrogate localization functional yields transductive excess-risk bounds that match the fixed-point and confidence structure of the classical LRC-based inductive bounds without the additional logarithmic confidence gap in existing works. We further advance transductive learning through two applications. First, for realizable transductive learning over a binary-valued class of VC dimension $2\le d <\infty$ with $u\ge m\ge d$, where $u$ and $m$ are the test and training sizes, STLC gives the upper bound $O(d\log(me/d)/m}$. This rate matches the classical LRC-based, standard ERM-style inductive upper bound. It remains a logarithmic factor $\log(me/d)$ above both the optimal realizable inductive PAC rate and the transductive minimax lower bound, which are of order $d/m$. Our prior work achieves the excess risk of $O(d/m)$ in a transductive setup by randomized learning. Second, STLC gives a sharper, spectrum-adaptive excess-risk bound for transductive kernel learning than the prior local-complexity-based result.
item.dc:creator: Yingzhen Yang

item.title: Undirected Multiple-Unicast Network Coding and Faster External-Memory Integer Sorting
item.description: arXiv:2610.20079v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In undirected multiple-unicast networks, where independent messages are sent between specified source-destination pairs, network coding allows intermediate nodes to combine messages, whereas fractional routing splits and forwards individual messages along paths without mixing them. Proposed in 2004 by Li and Li and independently by Harvey, Kleinberg, and Lehman, the multiple-unicast conjecture---long a central open problem in network coding with deep connections to computational complexity---asserts that network coding and fractional routing have the same achievable rate region. We construct a counterexample refuting this conjecture and use it to reduce block transfers in external-memory data rearrangement, thereby accelerating external-memory integer sorting and answering in the affirmative the longstanding question of Aggarwal and Vitter (1988) on whether integer operations can beat the comparison-sorting input/output (I/O) bound. Specifically, we give a deterministic sorting algorithm: for $N$ integers of $\Theta(\log N)$ bits, a memory holding $M$ integers, and block transfers of $B$ integers, where $2B\le M\le N$, the number of block transfers is $$O\!\left(\frac{N}{B}\left[1+\frac{\log N}{(\log(M/B))^{1-\varepsilon}(\log M)^\varepsilon}\right]\right),$$ where $\varepsilon=1.5\times10^{-5}$ is an absolute constant. This bound asymptotically improves on the classical $\Theta\!\left(\frac{N}{B}\left[1+\frac{\log(N/M)}{\log(M/B)}\right]\right)$ comparison-sorting bound in certain parameter regimes. Under the external-memory model specified in this paper, we have formally verified the algorithm's correctness and I/O complexity bound in Lean 4. Our reduction is independent of the address-field interchange construction. Using the one from recent work on multitape integer multiplication gives the bound for every fixed $0<\varepsilon<1/2$, with an $\varepsilon$-dependent constant.
item.dc:creator: Baochun Li, Zongpeng Li, Sirui Liu

item.title: Researcher-in-the-Loop Evolutionary Discovery of Entanglement-Assisted Quantum Code Families
item.description: arXiv:2610.41183v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: LLM-guided program evolution can produce mathematical constructions, but validity, generality, and reproducibility require distinct evidence. In this paper, we develop a researcher-in-the-loop discovery pipeline combining program evolution, exact evaluation, mathematical generalization, and independent verification. We apply it to entanglement-assisted quantum error-correcting codes (EAQECCs). Evolved programs produced finite qubit constructions from specifications that supplied no family formula. Researcher-directed analysis with a language model led to a general construction and proof drafts, which the researchers revised and checked. The resulting family $[[n,1,n-1;n-q-1]]_q$ exists for prime powers $q\ge3$ at $n\ge2q+1$ and for $q=2$ at odd $n\ge5$; Lean checks its formalized algebraic core. With entanglement lifting, it closes 54 listed table gaps. The evidence includes 115 verified code records, ten DRAT-checked nonexistence results, family implementations and preserved search programs. Controlled studies test how research proposals interact with program generation. Under a mutation-and-restart proposal, iterative evolution improves normalized success-curve area in all ten paired runs and raises success at excluded lengths $n=13,15$ from 13.4% to 62.5% and from 0.9% to 33.4%, respectively. The benefit depends on the proposal. Selected programs combine the proposed moves with objective and restart-counter changes. The pipeline connects finite computational discoveries to a proved family and independently checkable constructions.
item.dc:creator: Jae-Hyun Baek, Byung-Sun Won, Jon-Lark Kim

item.title: Karhunen-Lo\`eve Transforms of Autoregressive Windows Based on Matched Symmetry Groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.11624v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The Karhunen-Lo\`eve transform of a window of a stationary autoregressive process of any order $p$ is described through its poles, extending the Algebraic Diversity framework, which selects a transform by the matched group. For simple roots every basis vector is a sum of at most $p$ sinusoids, at the frequencies where the spectrum equals the eigenvalue, plus modes decaying from the ends. The window covariance differs from a member of the class diagonalized by the type-II discrete cosine transform by a closed-form matrix of rank $2p$, exactly when no pole is zero, so the eigenvalues interlace spectrum samples on the cosine grid, and the coding-gain loss of the cosine transform is an exact function of that matrix, below 1.2 percent for the $8\times8$ Markov block at pole $0.95$. By Kronecker's theorem the rank is at most $2\max(p,q)$ for rational spectra. A moving-average window departs in its Hankel corners, and an integrated (ARIMA) window departs by low rank from the type-VII sine class, exactly for the random walk. The exact symmetry is generically the reflection and contains a wreath product for interleaved windows. The dihedral group of the even extension is matched approximately, the dominant pole's sign choosing cosine or sine. The two groups give the transform a fast form: a parity fold, half-length cosine cores and a cascade of at most $p$ first-order Cauchy stages, exactly $p$ for a minimal AR($p$) model. The first-order case recovers results obtained by other means. This version adds complex data on the cyclic group with a border departure of rank exactly $2p$, the mixed and integrated classes, odd-length cores, and a released implementation whose kernel evaluation counts are flat in $M\log_2(M/n_{\mathrm{leaf}})$ to 5.3 percent. Experiments on recorded acoustic-array, radar and vibration data state where the transform helps and where existing methods match it.
item.dc:creator: Mitchell A. Thornton

item.title: A Fused Gaussian Process Bandit Framework for Multi-Fidelity Bayesian Optimization
item.description: arXiv:2611.32092v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Bayesian optimization (BO) is widely used to maximize expensive black-box functions when direct evaluation is costly. In many real-world applications, the high-fidelity objective can be approximated by a series of lower-fidelity models that provide partial but informative signals at substantially reduced cost. Multi-fidelity BO (MFBO) algorithms aim to strategically combine these information sources to achieve an optimal trade-off between accuracy and evaluation cost. However, existing MFBO methods often oversimplify the complex dependencies between fidelity levels or rely on heuristic acquisition functions that lack theoretical performance guarantees. To address these limitations, we introduce a new formulation of the MFBO problem as a fused Gaussian Process bandit and develop a corresponding Fused Gaussian Process Upper Confidence Bound (FGP-UCB) algorithm. Our approach accurately predicts the high-fidelity function by fusing multi-fidelity observations through an autoregressive Gaussian Process model and explicitly quantifies the uncertainty arising from parameter estimation across fidelity levels. The proposed method also provides theoretical simple-regret guarantees, overcoming a key limitation of existing MFBO algorithms that lack provable performance bounds. Effectiveness of the proposed method is demonstrated via both theoretical analysis and empirical studies.
item.dc:creator: Muyun Lu, Jose E Aguilar Escamilla, Huazheng Wang, Ying Lin
